criteria.text: Prophylaxis to prevent HAE attacks due to C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency (HAE-C1-INH) type 1 or 2.
Patient is 12 years of age or older (FDA labeled age).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an allergist or immunologist.
Dawnzera will not be used in combination with another agent indicated for HAE prophylaxis (denial criterion 2).
Patient has a documented history of 3 or more moderate to severe HAE attacks per month.
Medications with an established link to angioedema (e.g. ACE inhibitors, estrogen replacement therapy) have been evaluated and discontinued where appropriate.
Patient has tried and failed or has a documented clinical contraindication to at least two preferred agents approved for HAE prophylaxis from two different therapeutic classes.

notes: Partial encoding from AK Dawnzera (donidalorsen), a prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide, Criteria Version 1: Original 10/10/2025; Accepted 11/21/2025; Effective 01/01/2026.

The closed indication covers both diagnosis of HAE-C1-INH type 1 or 2 and use for HAE prophylaxis; no duplicate diagnosis or prophylaxis-only attestation is required. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria; denial criterion 2 excludes combination HAE prophylaxis.
Duration notes only: initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization approval up to 1 year.
Quantity notes only: 1 80mg autoinjector per 28 days.

Cautions (notes only): safety in pregnancy or breastfeeding has not been determined. The most common adverse reactions include injection site reactions, upper respiratory tract infection, urinary tract infection, and abdominal discomfort.
Documentation, duration, quantity enforcement and cautions require manual review; this pack remains partial.

Andembry is linked as an HAE prophylaxis alternative and requires separate evaluation of its one-preferred-agent step. Dawnzera requires at least two preferred agents from two different therapeutic classes.
